## Instructions

This quiz applies everything from Weeks 12-14. You'll practice selecting and interpreting statistical tests, including p-values and effect sizes. This is the last new content before your Research Plan is due.

---

## Part 1: Hypothesis Testing Logic

### Question 1: Null Hypothesis

The null hypothesis (H₀) typically predicts:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>A significant effect</option><option value='answer'>No effect or no difference</option><option value=''>The direction of the effect</option><option value=''>That the study will be successful</option></select>

Why do we test the null hypothesis rather than directly testing our experimental hypothesis?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The null is easier to understand</option><option value='answer'>We can calculate the probability of our data IF the null were true</option><option value=''>The experimental hypothesis is too complex</option><option value=''>It's just tradition</option></select>

### Question 2: p-Values

A p-value tells us:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The probability that the null hypothesis is true</option><option value=''>The probability that our hypothesis is correct</option><option value='answer'>The probability of obtaining our results (or more extreme) if the null hypothesis were true</option><option value=''>The effect size</option></select>

If p = .03, this means:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>There's a 3% chance our hypothesis is wrong</option><option value='answer'>There's a 3% chance of getting these results if there were no real effect</option><option value=''>The effect size is 3%</option><option value=''>3% of participants showed the effect</option></select>

### Question 3: Statistical Significance

We typically reject the null hypothesis when:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>p > .05</option><option value='answer'>p < .05</option><option value=''>p = .05</option><option value=''>p is any value</option></select>

A result with p = .08 is:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Statistically significant</option><option value='answer'>Not statistically significant at α = .05</option><option value=''>Definitely not a real effect</option><option value=''>A large effect</option></select>

---

## Part 2: t-Tests Applied

### Question 4: Choosing the Right t-Test

**Different participants** in each condition → <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>One-sample t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option></select>

**Same participants** measured twice → <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent t-test</option><option value='answer'>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>One-sample t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option></select>

### Question 5: DataLab t-Test Selection

**Room A vs Room B** reaction times (different students in each room):

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

**Pre-mood vs Post-mood** ratings (same students before and after):

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent t-test</option><option value='answer'>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

### Question 6: t-Test Assumptions

Which assumption applies to BOTH independent and paired t-tests?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Equal group sizes</option><option value='answer'>Data should be approximately normally distributed</option><option value=''>Participants must be matched on characteristics</option><option value=''>Correlation between variables</option></select>

The independent t-test additionally assumes:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Homogeneity of variance (similar SDs in both groups)</option><option value=''>Repeated measures</option><option value=''>Perfect normal distribution</option><option value=''>Large effect size</option></select>

---

## Part 3: Effect Size

### Question 7: Why Effect Size Matters

Effect size tells us:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Whether the result is significant</option><option value=''>The p-value</option><option value='answer'>The magnitude or practical importance of the difference</option><option value=''>The sample size needed</option></select>

A statistically significant result with a tiny effect size means:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The finding is very important</option><option value='answer'>The effect is real but may not be practically meaningful</option><option value=''>We should ignore the result</option><option value=''>The sample was too small</option></select>

### Question 8: Cohen's d Interpretation

Cohen's d = 0.2 is considered: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Small</option><option value=''>Medium</option><option value=''>Large</option><option value=''>Very large</option></select>

Cohen's d = 0.5 is considered: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value='answer'>Medium</option><option value=''>Large</option><option value=''>Very large</option></select>

Cohen's d = 0.8 is considered: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value=''>Medium</option><option value='answer'>Large</option><option value=''>Very large</option></select>

### Question 9: Effect Size Calculation

Cohen's d is calculated as:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Mean divided by SD</option><option value='answer'>Difference between means divided by pooled SD</option><option value=''>SD divided by mean</option><option value=''>Sample size divided by variance</option></select>

---

## Part 4: Interpreting Output

### Question 10: Reading Results

A t-test output shows: t(48) = 2.35, p = .023, d = 0.67

Is this result statistically significant at α = .05? <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

The effect size is: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value='answer'>Medium</option><option value=''>Large</option><option value=''>Cannot tell</option></select>

The degrees of freedom (df) are: <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='2' data-answer='["48"]'/>

### Question 11: APA Reporting

The correct APA format for reporting a t-test is:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>t = 2.35, significant</option><option value='answer'>t(48) = 2.35, p = .023, d = 0.67</option><option value=''>t-test was significant at .05 level</option><option value=''>The groups were different (t = 2.35)</option></select>

### Question 12: Correlation Reporting

A correlation analysis shows: r(38) = .45, p = .003

This represents a <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Weak</option><option value='answer'>Moderate to strong</option><option value=''>Perfect</option><option value=''>Non-significant</option></select> positive relationship.

The result IS statistically significant. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

---

## Part 5: Complete Test Selection

### Question 13: Design to Test Matching

Fill in the correct test for each scenario:

Comparing **two groups of different people**: <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='26' data-answer='["independent t-test","independent t test","independent samples t-test"]'/>

Comparing the **same people at two time points**: <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='21' data-answer='["paired t-test","paired t test","paired samples t-test","related t-test"]'/>

Examining the **relationship between two continuous variables**: <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='19' data-answer='["Pearson's r","Pearsons r","pearson","correlation","Pearson correlation"]'/>

### Question 14: Non-Parametric Alternatives

When data violate normality assumptions:

Independent t-test → <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Mann-Whitney U</option><option value=''>Wilcoxon signed-rank</option><option value=''>Spearman's rho</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

Paired t-test → <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Mann-Whitney U</option><option value='answer'>Wilcoxon signed-rank</option><option value=''>Spearman's rho</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

Pearson's r → <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Mann-Whitney U</option><option value=''>Wilcoxon signed-rank</option><option value='answer'>Spearman's rho</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

---

## Part 6: MCQ Exam Practice

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 1

A researcher tests whether a mindfulness intervention reduces stress. 30 participants are randomly assigned to either a mindfulness group or a control group. Stress is measured after 4 weeks.

1. **Design**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option><option value=''>Correlational</option></select>

2. **IV**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Group (mindfulness vs control)</option><option value=''>Stress level</option><option value=''>Time (4 weeks)</option><option value=''>No IV</option></select>

3. **DV**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Group assignment</option><option value='answer'>Stress level</option><option value=''>Mindfulness practice</option><option value=''>Participant age</option></select>

4. **Appropriate test**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>Mann-Whitney U</option></select>

5. **Results: t(28) = 2.89, p = .007, d = 1.08. This is**:
   - Significant? <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>
   - Effect size: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value=''>Medium</option><option value='answer'>Large</option><option value=''>Cannot determine</option></select>

6. **The correct conclusion is**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>The mindfulness group had significantly lower stress than controls</option><option value=''>There was no significant difference</option><option value=''>The control group had lower stress</option><option value=''>We cannot draw any conclusions</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 2

A researcher measures students' confidence before and after receiving exam feedback.

1. **Design**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value='answer'>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option><option value=''>Correlational</option></select>

2. **IV**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Time (before vs after feedback)</option><option value=''>Confidence level</option><option value=''>Exam grade</option><option value=''>No IV</option></select>

3. **DV**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Time point</option><option value='answer'>Confidence level</option><option value=''>Feedback content</option><option value=''>Student ID</option></select>

4. **Appropriate test**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent t-test</option><option value='answer'>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>Wilcoxon signed-rank</option></select>

5. **Results: t(24) = -3.45, p = .002, d = 0.69. The negative t-value means**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The result is not significant</option><option value='answer'>Confidence decreased (before > after)</option><option value=''>The calculation is wrong</option><option value=''>The effect size is negative</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### Investigation 3

A researcher examines whether study hours predict exam scores in 60 students.

1. **Design**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option><option value='answer'>Correlational</option></select>

2. **IV**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Study hours</option><option value=''>Exam scores</option><option value=''>Number of students</option><option value='answer'>No IV</option></select>

3. **Appropriate test**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value='answer'>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>ANOVA</option></select>

4. **Results: r(58) = .52, p < .001. This represents**: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>A weak relationship</option><option value='answer'>A moderate to strong positive relationship</option><option value=''>No relationship</option><option value=''>A negative relationship</option></select>

5. **Can we conclude studying CAUSES better grades?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

:::

## Summary Checklist

Before moving on, make sure you can:

- [ ] Explain the logic of hypothesis testing (null hypothesis, p-value)
- [ ] Interpret p-values correctly (NOT the probability the null is true)
- [ ] Select the appropriate test for any design (independent t, paired t, Pearson's r)
- [ ] Identify non-parametric alternatives
- [ ] Interpret and report effect sizes (Cohen's d, r)
- [ ] Read and interpret statistical output
- [ ] Report results in APA format
